note: The random sources: four class rows and their seed round trips. The SEQUENCE is deliberately not a row: the ledger and the facts entry say the release's generators are not identified, so no sequence is claimed.

entries.reason: the release has no GameplayKit at all: the armv7 shared cache of 6.1.3 carries no such class, and the 16.4 SDK declares it at 8.0. The class is carried because it is pure CPU logic, and the sequence it produces is the standard algorithm, NOT the release's own: the release's sequences are not the standard algorithms, measured black-box against the host's own GameplayKit (dladdr on the IMP BY NAME: every answer comes from GameplayKit.framework/Versions/A/GameplayKit; dladdr on the call's function pointer returns nothing under Catalyst, which is why the IMP is taken by name). Mersenne Twister, seed 5489, -nextInt x4: the host -915597028 1075804871 -1242657610 -229060051 against MT19937 1351727964 581869302 1742863086 1438850937; seeds 1, 12345 and 3735928559 differ the same way; the scalings (raw, & 0x7fffffff, >> 1, an int32 cast) and the seedings (init_genrand, init_by_array, init_by_array with four words) are all measured and all differ, and the host's values are full 32-bit signed, so the masking is unidentified too. ARC4, seed the 15 bytes "charon-arc4-seed": the host -268849773 560625053 -478456873 -465298256 against RC4 330168815 494234145 1465088995 807159012, and still different after -dropValuesWithCount: 1536 and with the seed zero-padded to a 16-byte key. Linear congruential, seed 1: the host 384748 3143714957 3745583449; recovering (a, c) from the host's own consecutive outputs gives a=3096923468 c=3630308989 and predicts a fourth draw of 3848931817 where the host says 1612966641, so the transition is not x = a*x + c over the full 32 bits; neither classic matches (1664525/1013904223 gives 1015568748 1586005467 2165703038, glibc's 1103515245/12345 gives 1103527590 2524885223 662824084). OWED: identify the release's three generators, and the scaling nextInt applies. Until then the port carries the standard algorithm for each, deterministic and seeded the way its own header says, and no sequence row is claimed.

entries.effect: each distribution draws through the source it was given: -nextInt asks for the whole range and adds the lowest, -nextBool is the source's own, -nextUniform is that integer over the highest and so is quantised, and -nextIntWithUpperBound: asks for the bound less the lowest, never more than the whole range, and for the whole range when the bound is zero -- all measured over the host with a written script; a gaussian takes the middle of a range and a sixth of it, or three deviations around a mean, and asks for two uniforms per draw; a shuffled one shuffles forward once per pass and hands the values out from the back; and -init is the degenerate distribution over zero and zero

entries.effect: each distribution draws through the source it was given: -nextInt asks for the whole range and adds the lowest, -nextBool is the source's own, -nextUniform is that integer over the highest and so is quantised, and -nextIntWithUpperBound: asks for the bound less the lowest, never more than the whole range, and for the whole range when the bound is zero -- all measured over the host with a written script; a gaussian takes the middle of a range and a sixth of it, or three deviations around a mean, and asks for two uniforms per draw; a shuffled one shuffles forward once per pass and hands the values out from the back; and -init is the degenerate distribution over zero and zero
